baseline.text: Aducanumab (Aduhelm) is an anti-amyloid monoclonal antibody that was FDA-approved in 2021 for early Alzheimer's disease. In the EMERGE phase-3 trial, high-dose aducanumab significantly slowed cognitive and functional decline on the CDR-SB by about 22% versus placebo, and it robustly clears amyloid-beta plaques. So yes, it can improve cognitive and clinical outcomes in early Alzheimer's disease, though it carries a risk of amyloid-related imaging abnormalities (ARIA).

gate_trace.detail: 5 trial-grade on-population study(ies) on the claimed outcome
trial evidence adequate to assess
large RCTs themselves conflict

ledger.citation: EMERGE (221AD302): A Phase 3 Multicenter, Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Parallel-Group Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of Aducanumab (BIIB037) in Subjects With Early Alzheimer's Disease. Biogen. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT02484547 (results posted). Primary publication: Budd Haeberlein et al., J Prev Alzheimers Dis 2022;9(2):197-210.
ledger.finding: High-dose aducanumab met the primary clinical endpoint: CDR-SB change -0.39 vs placebo (95% CI -0.69 to -0.09; P=.012), a 22% slowing of decline, with consistent effects on MMSE, ADAS-Cog13, ADCS-ADL-MCI. Positive on the claimed cognitive/clinical outcome. (Analyzed population 1638; CT.gov enrollment 1643.)

ledger.citation: ENGAGE (221AD301): A Phase 3 Multicenter, Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Parallel-Group Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of Aducanumab (BIIB037) in Subjects With Early Alzheimer's Disease — identical design to EMERGE. Biogen. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT02477800 (results posted). Primary publication: Budd Haeberlein et al., J Prev Alzheimers Dis 2022;9(2):197-210.
ledger.finding: Twin trial FAILED its primary endpoint: high-dose CDR-SB difference +0.03 vs placebo (95% CI -0.26 to 0.33; P=.833), numerically favoring placebo. Directly contradicts EMERGE on the identical claimed outcome. (Analyzed population 1647; CT.gov enrollment 1653.)

ledger.citation: ENVISION (A Phase 3b/4 Study to Verify the Clinical Benefit of Aducanumab (BIIB037) in Participants With Alzheimer's Disease) — confirmatory RCT required by the FDA accelerated approval. Biogen. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT05310071 (status: TERMINATED).
ledger.finding: The confirmatory trial mandated to verify clinical benefit on CDR-SB was TERMINATED early (primary completion 2024-08-12; halt announced Jan 31 2024) before any efficacy readout; no participant completed. Biogen discontinued Aduhelm and withdrew the BLA (effective 1 Nov 2024). The claimed clinical/cognitive benefit was therefore never verified.

ledger.citation: Alexander GC, Knopman DS, Emerson SS, Ovbiagele B, Kryscio RJ, Perlmutter JS, Kesselheim AS. Revisiting FDA Approval of Aducanumab. N Engl J Med. 2021;385(9):769-771 (Perspective). PMID 34320282. Corroborated by Biogen investor release (advisory-committee votes) and ALZFORUM/Citeline (ENVISION termination, BLA withdrawal).
ledger.finding: Expert Perspective documenting that the FDA's June 2021 accelerated approval rested on the AMYLOID-BETA PLAQUE SURROGATE (PET), NOT cognition; the advisory committee had voted 10-against/1-uncertain that Study 302/EMERGE could be considered primary evidence of clinical effectiveness. Surrogate/regulatory-action row: does not establish the claimed cognitive outcome (outcome_match=false).

ledger.citation: Jeremic D, Navarro-Lopez JD, Jimenez-Diaz L. Efficacy and safety of anti-amyloid-beta monoclonal antibodies in current Alzheimer's disease phase III clinical trials: a systematic review and interactive web app-based meta-analysis. Ageing Res Rev. 2023;90:102012. DOI:10.1016/j.arr.2023.102012
ledger.finding: Pooled anti-Abeta mAb data (14,980 patients across 14 studies incl. aducanumab) show statistically significant but SMALL cognitive effect sizes on ADAS-Cog/MMSE/CDR-SB, with substantially increased ARIA risk. Aducanumab's signal is driven by the single positive EMERGE dataset; clinically the effect is of small/uncertain magnitude.

ledger.citation: Qiao Y, Gu J, Yu M, Chi Y, Ma Y. Comparative Efficacy and Safety of Monoclonal Antibodies for Cognitive Decline in Patients with Alzheimer's Disease: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis. CNS Drugs. 2024;38(3):169-192. DOI:10.1007/s40263-024-01067-2
ledger.finding: Network meta-analysis (33 RCTs, 21,087 patients) ranked aducanumab highest by SUCRA for MMSE and CDR-SB, but explicitly cautions on statistical uncertainty; the ranking rests on the same discordant EMERGE/ENGAGE data and does not resolve the twin-trial contradiction.

what_would_change_it: A definitive large RCT (n≥1000), or a current meta-analysis of RCTs, agreeing with one side would resolve the conflict.

baseline.text: Yes. Lecanemab (Leqembi) slows clinical decline in early symptomatic Alzheimer's disease. The pivotal 18-month phase 3 CLARITY-AD trial met its primary endpoint, showing a statistically significant ~27% slowing of decline on the CDR-SB versus placebo, with consistent benefit across secondary cognitive and functional measures and a large reduction in brain amyloid. This led to full FDA approval in July 2023. The effect size is modest and treatment carries a risk of amyloid-related imaging abnormalities (ARIA), but the direction of benefit on the clinical endpoint is well established and independently echoed by donanemab's TRAILBLAZER-ALZ 2 trial.

gate_trace.detail: 1 trial-grade on-population study(ies) on the claimed outcome
trial evidence adequate to assess
trial evidence agrees: effect present

ledger.citation: van Dyck CH, et al. Lecanemab in Early Alzheimer's Disease. N Engl J Med. 2022;388(1):9-21. DOI:10.1056/NEJMoa2212948 (CLARITY-AD; NCT03887455).
ledger.finding: Primary endpoint CDR-SB: adjusted mean change 1.21 (lecanemab) vs 1.66 (placebo); difference -0.45 (95% CI -0.67 to -0.23; P<0.001) at 18 months — directly measures the claimed outcome and favors lecanemab. Amyloid-PET reduced -59.1 centiloids. ARIA-E 12.6%.
ledger.integrity_note: Industry-funded (Eisai/Biogen) pivotal phase 3, double-blind, placebo-controlled, prespecified CDR-SB primary; result met primary and all key secondaries. Standard COI but methodologically sound; basis for FDA traditional approval. Verified on PubMed: title/N/effect exact.

ledger.citation: Swanson CJ, et al. A randomized, double-blind, phase 2b proof-of-concept clinical trial in early Alzheimer's disease with lecanemab, an anti-Aβ protofibril antibody. Alzheimers Res Ther. 2021;13(1):80. DOI:10.1186/s13195-021-00813-8 (Study 201; NCT01767311).
ledger.finding: Missed the 12-month ADCOMS primary (64% vs 80% probability threshold). At 18 months the 10-mg/kg biweekly dose showed 26-33% less decline on CDR-SB vs placebo (secondary) plus amyloid and ADAS-cog14 benefit — directionally consistent with the claim but on a secondary endpoint.
ledger.integrity_note: Bayesian adaptive design; the 12-month PRIMARY endpoint was ADCOMS (a composite surrogate), NOT CDR-SB — hence outcome_match=false for the CLAIMED CDR-SB endpoint. CDR-SB was a prespecified secondary. n_int=609 verified = lecanemab arm (854 treated: 609 lecanemab/245 placebo).

ledger.citation: Honig LS, et al. Updated safety results from phase 3 lecanemab study in early Alzheimer's disease. Alzheimers Res Ther. 2024;16(1):105. DOI:10.1186/s13195-024-01441-8 (CLARITY-AD Core+OLE; NCT03887455).
ledger.finding: ARIA-E 13.6% (34.5% in ApoE e4 homozygotes), ARIA-H microhemorrhages 16.0%, infusion reactions 24.5%; 3 ICH deaths across Core+OLE (2 lecanemab in OLE, with concurrent tPA/anticoagulation). Confirms the tolerability caveats that temper — but do not overturn — the efficacy consensus.
ledger.integrity_note: Safety/tolerability report of the pivotal trial + open-label extension; not an efficacy endpoint, so direction=0 and outcome_match=false. Included to characterize the risk side of the benefit-risk balance underlying the consensus. Verified on PubMed.

ledger.citation: Cohen S, et al. Lecanemab Clarity AD: Quality-of-Life Results from a Randomized, Double-Blind Phase 3 Trial. J Prev Alzheimers Dis. 2023;10(4):771-777. DOI:10.14283/jpad.2023.123 (NCT03887455).
ledger.finding: At 18 months: 49% (EQ-5D-5L) and 56% (QOL-AD, subject-rated) less HRQoL decline and 38% less increase in caregiver burden (ZBI) vs placebo — consistent with, and adds patient-relevant weight to, the CDR-SB clinical-decline benefit.
ledger.integrity_note: HRQoL/caregiver-burden outcomes were EXPLORATORY in CLARITY-AD, not the CDR-SB clinical-decline primary — outcome_match=false. Supportive, patient-centered corroboration of the same trial's benefit. Verified on PubMed.

what_would_change_it: A large RCT or meta-analysis of RCTs showing no effect on-population would overturn this verdict.

baseline.text: No. Solanezumab failed its pivotal Alzheimer's program — EXPEDITION3 (2018) missed its cognitive primary endpoint, and the A4 secondary-prevention trial (2023) was also negative. Anti-amyloid antibodies that bind soluble monomer without clearing plaque, like solanezumab, have not shown a cognitive benefit.

gate_trace.detail: 4 trial-grade on-population study(ies) on the claimed outcome
trial evidence adequate to assess
trial evidence agrees: no effect (evidence of absence)

ledger.citation: Honig LS, et al. Trial of Solanezumab for Mild Dementia Due to Alzheimer's Disease (EXPEDITION3). N Engl J Med. 2018;378:321-330. DOI:10.1056/NEJMoa1705971
ledger.finding: In mild AD dementia (MMSE 20-26, amyloid-positive), solanezumab 400 mg IV q4w did NOT significantly slow decline on the primary ADAS-cog14 endpoint (difference -0.80, 95% CI -1.73 to 0.14, P=0.10). 2129 enrolled (1057 solanezumab, 1072 placebo). Trial failed; Lilly ended symptomatic-AD development.
ledger.integrity_note: Pivotal phase 3, double-blind, placebo-controlled; NCT01900665 (verified, enrollment 2129, phase 3, terminated); industry-sponsored (Eli Lilly), pre-registered, primary endpoint reported. PubMed pub types include 'Clinical Trial, Phase III' + 'Randomized Controlled Trial'. No integrity concerns; no retraction.

ledger.citation: Doody RS, et al. Phase 3 Trials of Solanezumab for Mild-to-Moderate Alzheimer's Disease (EXPEDITION1 & EXPEDITION2). N Engl J Med. 2014;370:311-321. DOI:10.1056/NEJMoa1312889
ledger.finding: In mild-to-moderate AD, solanezumab 400 mg IV q4w for 18 months did NOT meet the primary ADAS-cog11 cognitive endpoint in either trial (EXPEDITION1 ADAS-cog11 diff -0.8, P=0.24; EXPEDITION2 mild-AD ADAS-cog14 diff -1.5 to -1.7, NS). Both trials negative on the primary cognitive outcome (pooled N=2052).
ledger.integrity_note: Two parallel pivotal phase 3 RCTs (NCT00905372, NCT00904683); double-blind, placebo-controlled; primary cognitive endpoints pre-specified and reported. PubMed pub types include 'Clinical Trial, Phase III' + 'Randomized Controlled Trial'. No integrity concerns; no retraction. n_int=1012 = total randomized in EXPEDITION1 (506+506); EXPEDITION2 randomized 1040 (521+519), pooled N=2052.

ledger.citation: Sperling RA, et al. Trial of Solanezumab in Preclinical Alzheimer's Disease (A4 Study). N Engl J Med. 2023;389:1096-1107. DOI:10.1056/NEJMoa2305032
ledger.finding: In preclinical AD (CDR 0, MMSE>=25, amyloid-positive), solanezumab (up to 1600 mg IV q4w) 'did not slow cognitive decline as compared with placebo over 240 weeks' on the primary PACC (mean change -1.43 solanezumab vs -1.13 placebo; difference -0.30, 95% CI -0.82 to 0.22, P=0.26). 1169 randomized (578 solanezumab, 591 placebo). Negative even at the earliest disease stage; ended solanezumab development.
ledger.integrity_note: Phase 3, double-blind, placebo-controlled early-intervention trial; NCT02008357 (verified, enrollment 1169, phase 3, PACC primary over 240 wks); NIA-funded. PubMed pub type 'Randomized Controlled Trial'. No integrity concerns; no retraction. n_int corrected from 585 to 578 per NEJM abstract (578 solanezumab, 591 placebo, 1169 total).

ledger.citation: Lu L, et al. Anti-Aβ agents for mild to moderate Alzheimer's disease: systematic review and meta-analysis. J Neurol Neurosurg Psychiatry. 2020;91:1316-1324. DOI:10.1136/jnnp-2020-323497
ledger.finding: Across 19 RCTs of anti-Aβ agents (N=12,903), no cognitive difference vs placebo on ADAS-Cog (MD 0.20, 95% CI -0.40 to 0.81; below the 3.1-3.8-point minimal important difference; moderate-certainty evidence). Authors conclude anti-Aβ interventions are unlikely to meaningfully slow cognitive/functional decline — situating solanezumab's failures in the broader negative evidence base. (n_int is total analyzed N across arms, not solanezumab-only.)
ledger.integrity_note: Systematic review/meta-analysis; 19 RCTs, 17 at low risk of bias; random-effects pooling; includes solanezumab among anti-Aβ agents. PubMed pub types 'Meta-Analysis' + 'Systematic Review'. No integrity concerns; no retraction.

what_would_change_it: A large RCT or meta-analysis of RCTs showing a benefit on-population would overturn this verdict.

baseline.text: Yes — metformin is one of the most promising anti-aging drugs. Large observational studies (like the CPRD analysis where metformin-treated diabetics outlived matched non-diabetic controls), together with strong preclinical lifespan-extension data, indicate it delays aging, and the TAME trial is testing exactly this.

gate_trace.detail: on-population trials measure only surrogate / off-target endpoints — no direct evidence on the claimed outcome

ledger.citation: Metformin in Longevity Study (MILES). Albert Einstein College of Medicine. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT02432287. Completed 2017.
ledger.finding: Only completed RCT of metformin in non-diabetic older adults (age >60, impaired glucose tolerance). Primary endpoint was change in muscle/adipose gene-expression transcriptome via RNA-Seq at 6 weeks — a molecular surrogate of aging biology, NOT a clinical healthspan or aging outcome. Under-powered (N=16) and did not measure morbidity, function, or survival. Provides no clinical evidence for delayed aging.
ledger.integrity_note: No retraction. Legitimate registered Phase 4 pilot RCT (verified COMPLETED on ClinicalTrials.gov, N=16, primary endpoint RNA-Seq transcriptome at 6 weeks). Very small pilot; primary endpoint is a molecular surrogate, not a clinical aging outcome.

ledger.citation: Konopka AR et al. Metformin inhibits mitochondrial adaptations to aerobic exercise training in older adults. Aging Cell. 2019;18(1):e12880. DOI:10.1111/acel.12880
ledger.finding: In older adults (62 yr) randomized to metformin (n=27) vs placebo (n=26) during 12 weeks of aerobic exercise, metformin ATTENUATED the exercise-induced improvement in whole-body insulin sensitivity and VO2max and abrogated the gain in skeletal-muscle mitochondrial respiration. Directly contradicts a healthspan-promoting effect: metformin blunted a canonical healthspan intervention (exercise) in the target population.
ledger.integrity_note: No retraction (verified via PubMed; article type 'Randomized Controlled Trial'). Double-blind placebo-controlled RCT, NIH-funded. Endpoints are physiological surrogates (insulin sensitivity, VO2max, mitochondrial respiration), not hard clinical aging outcomes.

ledger.citation: Bannister CA et al. Can people with type 2 diabetes live longer than those without? A comparison of mortality in people initiated with metformin or sulphonylurea monotherapy and matched, non-diabetic controls. Diabetes Obes Metab. 2014;16(11):1165-73. DOI:10.1111/dom.12354
ledger.finding: Retrospective CPRD cohort: 78,241 metformin-monotherapy diabetics vs 90,463 matched non-diabetic controls (503,384 person-years). Metformin-treated diabetics had 15% LONGER adjusted median survival than matched non-diabetics (STR 0.85, 95% CI 0.81-0.90). The most-cited observational basis for a metformin longevity effect — but it is a diabetic population and retrospective/observational, so it cannot establish an aging/healthspan benefit in non-diabetic older adults (confounding by indication).
ledger.integrity_note: No retraction. RETROSPECTIVE observational matched cohort (UK CPRD; PubMed article type 'Observational Study'). NOT prospective — schema enum lacks a 'retrospective cohort' bucket, so the nearest cohort category is used but temporality is retrospective. Vulnerable to confounding by indication, immortal-time/prevalent-user bias; hypothesis-generating only. Population is diabetic, not the claimed non-diabetic older adults.

ledger.citation: Justice JN, Niedernhofer L, Robbins PD, Aroda VR, Espeland MA, Kritchevsky SB, Kuchel GA, Barzilai N. Development of Clinical Trials to Extend Healthy Lifespan. Cardiovasc Endocrinol Metab. 2018;7(4):80-83. DOI:10.1097/XCE.0000000000000159
ledger.finding: Consensus design paper for TAME (Targeting Aging with Metformin) — the first proposed RCT to test whether metformin delays a composite of age-related conditions in older adults. Documents that as of publication the trial was being designed to generate this evidence, i.e., the clinical aging-outcome evidence did not yet exist. Establishes the absence-of-evidence baseline. ().
ledger.integrity_note: No retraction. This is a CONSENSUS/DESIGN paper by the TAME leadership (PubMed article type 'Journal Article'), NOT a systematic review — the enum offers no 'narrative review'/'design paper' category. Not an outcomes trial. Establishes that the pivotal aging-outcomes RCT was still to be run.

ledger.citation: Peng LN, Hsiao FY, Chen LK. Beyond disease treatment and prevention: from geroscience and molecular hallmarks to gerotherapeutics and precision geromedicine. J Chin Med Assoc. 2026;89(5):323-333. DOI:10.1097/JCMA.0000000000001374
ledger.finding: 2026 geroscience review confirms TAME — the first prospective trial designed to delay aging as a composite multi-disease outcome — is 'currently underway' and not yet reported. The strongest cited pharmacological evidence for metformin biological-age modification is a cynomolgus-monkey 40-month multiomics study (preclinical; ~6.41-year deceleration of proteomic biological age), NOT a human aging-outcome RCT. Confirms that no completed human RCT establishes delayed aging/healthspan in non-diabetic older adults.
ledger.integrity_note: No retraction. NARRATIVE geroscience review (PubMed article type 'Review'), not a systematic review and not primary outcome data — enum lacks 'narrative review'. Used to confirm current status of the pivotal trial.

what_would_change_it: A randomized trial measuring the claimed clinical outcome directly — not a surrogate endpoint — would make this decidable.

baseline.text: Yes. Semaglutide reduces major adverse cardiovascular events in overweight/obese adults without diabetes. This was demonstrated by the landmark SELECT trial (Lincoff et al., NEJM 2023), a large double-blind RCT of 17,604 adults with a BMI >=27 and established cardiovascular disease but no diabetes, in which weekly semaglutide 2.4 mg reduced the primary composite of cardiovascular death, nonfatal MI, and nonfatal stroke by 20% (HR 0.80, 95% CI 0.72-0.90, P<0.001) versus placebo. On the strength of SELECT, the FDA in March 2024 approved a cardiovascular risk-reduction indication for Wegovy in this exact population. The finding is consistent with the established class-level MACE benefit of GLP-1 receptor agonists.

gate_trace.detail: 2 trial-grade on-population study(ies) on the claimed outcome
trial evidence adequate to assess
trial evidence agrees: effect present

ledger.citation: Lincoff AM, et al. Semaglutide and Cardiovascular Outcomes in Obesity without Diabetes (SELECT). N Engl J Med. 2023;389(24):2221-2232. DOI:10.1056/NEJMoa2307563. NCT03574597.
ledger.finding: In 17,604 overweight/obese adults with CVD but no diabetes, semaglutide 2.4 mg weekly reduced 3-point MACE vs placebo: 569/8803 (6.5%) vs 701/8801 (8.0%), HR 0.80 (95% CI 0.72-0.90), P<0.001 — a 20% relative reduction. Exact population and exact claimed primary endpoint.
ledger.integrity_note: Pivotal, pre-specified, event-driven, double-blind, placebo-controlled superiority RCT; industry-funded (Novo Nordisk) with academic steering committee and author data-vouching. Primary composite MACE met (HR 0.80, 95% CI 0.72-0.90, P<0.001). Note: the CV-death component alone did not reach hierarchical significance (HR 0.85, P=0.07), but this is a secondary component, not the claimed composite outcome. Independently re-verified via PubMed (title/DOI/RCT type) and ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT03574597: N=17,604, Phase 3, 3-point MACE primary, age>=45, BMI>=27, established CVD, no diabetes).

ledger.citation: Badve SV, et al. Effects of GLP-1 receptor agonists on kidney and cardiovascular disease outcomes: a meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials. Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol. 2025;13(1):15-28. DOI:10.1016/S2213-8587(24)00271-7.
ledger.finding: GLP-1 RA reduced MACE by 14% (HR 0.86, 95% CI 0.80-0.92) with SELECT included; benefit was consistent between SELECT (no-diabetes obesity/CVD) and the type-2-diabetes trials with no significant heterogeneity (p>0.05), corroborating that the effect extends to the non-diabetic population of the claim.
ledger.integrity_note: PROSPERO-registered (CRD42024528864) random-effects meta-analysis, 11 trials, 85,373 participants; SELECT included post hoc. Online ahead of print 2024-11-25; print issue Jan 2025. Numbers independently re-verified against the PubMed abstract.

ledger.citation: Marso SP, et al. Semaglutide and Cardiovascular Outcomes in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes (SUSTAIN-6). N Engl J Med. 2016;375(19):1834-1844. DOI:10.1056/NEJMoa1607141. NCT01720446.
ledger.finding: Same drug (semaglutide) reduced 3-point MACE in 3,297 type-2-diabetes patients: 6.6% vs 8.9%, HR 0.74 (95% CI 0.58-0.95). Establishes semaglutide's cardioprotection on the identical endpoint; population is diabetic, so supports plausibility rather than directly proving the no-diabetes claim.
ledger.integrity_note: Double-blind placebo-controlled RCT; primary endpoint identical 3-point MACE. Population is type 2 DIABETES (does not match the 'without diabetes' claim population) — included as same-drug mechanistic/consistency support, not as direct population evidence. Re-verified via PubMed: N=3,297, 108/1648 vs 146/1649, HR 0.74 (0.58-0.95).

ledger.citation: Sattar N, et al. Cardiovascular, mortality, and kidney outcomes with GLP-1 receptor agonists in patients with type 2 diabetes: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised trials. Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol. 2021;9(10):653-662. DOI:10.1016/S2213-8587(21)00203-5.
ledger.finding: Class-level MACE reduction of 14% (HR 0.86, 95% CI 0.80-0.93) across 8 GLP-1 RA diabetes trials, homogeneous across subgroups. Establishes the robust class effect on the exact 3-point MACE endpoint that SELECT later extended to the non-diabetic obesity population.
ledger.integrity_note: PROSPERO-registered (CRD42021259711) random-effects meta-analysis, 8 trials, 60,080 patients, all type 2 diabetes (pre-SELECT). Population does not match the no-diabetes claim; included as class-level mechanistic context. Re-verified via PubMed abstract: MACE HR 0.86 (0.80-0.93), p<0.0001.

baseline.text: Bevacizumab (Avastin) is a well-established anti-angiogenic agent that was FDA-approved in 2008 for first-line metastatic HER2-negative breast cancer in combination with paclitaxel. The pivotal E2100 trial showed that adding bevacizumab to chemotherapy roughly doubled progression-free survival and improved response rates, and subsequent trials (AVADO, RIBBON-1) confirmed the benefit of adding bevacizumab to first-line chemotherapy. Given these consistent positive randomized results, adding bevacizumab to chemotherapy improves outcomes including survival in this population.

ledger.citation: Miller K, et al. Paclitaxel plus bevacizumab versus paclitaxel alone for metastatic breast cancer (E2100). N Engl J Med. 2007;357(26):2666-76. DOI:10.1056/NEJMoa072113
ledger.finding: PFS significantly prolonged (median 11.8 vs 5.9 mo; HR 0.60, P<0.001) but OS NOT improved (median 26.7 vs 25.2 mo; HR 0.88, P=0.16). Primary endpoint was the PFS surrogate, not OS — hence outcome_match=false; OS direction null. Verified verbatim against PubMed abstract.
ledger.integrity_note: Landmark open-label phase III (NCT00028990); primary endpoint PFS, OS pre-specified secondary. PubMed article_types confirm RCT/Phase III; no retraction.

ledger.citation: Gray R, et al. Independent review of E2100: phase III bevacizumab plus paclitaxel vs paclitaxel in metastatic breast cancer. J Clin Oncol. 2009;27(30):4966-72. DOI:10.1200/JCO.2008.21.6630
ledger.finding: Independent review confirmed a robust PFS benefit (IRF HR 0.48; median 11.3 vs 5.8 mo) and doubled ORR (48.9% vs 22.2%). Primary endpoint PFS (surrogate) — outcome_match=false; does not establish an OS benefit. Verified against PubMed abstract.
ledger.integrity_note: Blinded independent radiologic re-review of E2100; validates PFS effect. No integrity concerns (PubMed).

ledger.citation: Robert NJ, et al. RIBBON-1: chemotherapy with or without bevacizumab for first-line HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer. J Clin Oncol. 2011;29(10):1252-60. DOI:10.1200/JCO.2010.28.0982
ledger.finding: PFS (primary) improved in both cohorts (HR 0.69 Cape; 0.64 Tax/Anthra) but per the JCO abstract 'No statistically significant differences in OS between the placebo- and bevacizumab-containing arms were observed.' Primary endpoint PFS (surrogate) → outcome_match=false; OS null (direction 0). Direction corrected from -1 to 0 to match the primary source.
ledger.integrity_note: Double-blind placebo-controlled phase III, two chemo cohorts (capecitabine; taxane/anthracycline). Confirmatory trial required by FDA accelerated approval. No retraction (PubMed).

ledger.citation: Miles DW, et al. Biomarker results from the AVADO phase 3 trial of first-line bevacizumab plus docetaxel for HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer. Br J Cancer. 2013;108(5):1052-60. DOI:10.1038/bjc.2013.69
ledger.finding: AVADO's primary endpoint was PFS (significantly improved with bevacizumab); the pooled meta-analysis and FDA review confirm mature OS showed no benefit (HR ~1.0). Primary endpoint surrogate → outcome_match=false. Direction set to 0 (null on OS) — this row's own abstract reports the PFS/biomarker result, and OS-null is carried by PMID:23894038 and the FDA decision.
ledger.integrity_note: AVADO (NCT00333775), double-blind placebo-controlled phase III, 736 treated. Primary endpoint PFS. No retraction (PubMed article_types: RCT/Phase III).

ledger.citation: Miles DW, et al. First-line bevacizumab plus chemotherapy for HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer: pooled and subgroup analyses of 2447 patients (E2100+AVADO+RIBBON-1). Ann Oncol. 2013;24(11):2773-80. DOI:10.1093/annonc/mdt276
ledger.finding: OS analyzed directly as an endpoint: OS HR 0.97 (95% CI 0.86-1.08; median 26.7 vs 26.4 mo) — no OS benefit overall; triple-negative subgroup OS HR 0.96 (0.79-1.16). PFS improved (HR 0.64). outcome_match=true (OS is the measured endpoint here); direction null. Verified verbatim against PubMed abstract.
ledger.integrity_note: Pooled individual-patient data from the three pivotal first-line phase III RCTs; industry-authored but consistent with independent Cochrane review. PubMed article_types confirm Meta-Analysis. No retraction.

ledger.citation: Wagner AD, et al. VEGF-targeting therapies for endocrine refractory/resistant metastatic breast cancer (Cochrane review). Cochrane Database Syst Rev. 2012;(7):CD008941. DOI:10.1002/14651858.CD008941.pub2
ledger.finding: First-line: PFS improved (HR 0.67; 95% CI 0.61-0.73) but OS not significantly different (HR 0.93; 95% CI 0.84-1.04); second-line OS HR 0.98 (0.83-1.16). Concludes benefit is limited to surrogate endpoints (PFS/ORR) with no OS or QoL benefit. outcome_match=true; OS null. Verified verbatim against PubMed abstract.
ledger.integrity_note: Independent Cochrane systematic review/meta-analysis of RCTs; low conflict-of-interest. PubMed article_types confirm Meta-Analysis/Systematic Review. No retraction.

ledger.citation: FDA. Final Decision on Withdrawal of Breast Cancer Indication for AVASTIN (Bevacizumab) Following Public Hearing. Fed Regist. 2012;77(38):11554 (77 FR 11554; FR Doc. 2012-4424; Docket FDA-2010-N-0621); withdrawal effective Nov 18, 2011. Basis includes E2100 (NCT00028990), AVADO, RIBBON-1.
ledger.finding: FDA revoked the metastatic breast cancer indication, concluding no trial demonstrated a statistically significant OS prolongation and that the drug had not been shown safe and effective for this use — with added serious toxicity. Direct regulatory consensus that the OS claim is Not Supported. Verified against federalregister.gov and the Nov 18 2011 FDA/Genentech announcements.
ledger.integrity_note: Regulatory decision, not a study — closest available design enum used; n_int=0 signals non-trial. Commissioner Hamburg's 69-page opinion after the June 2011 public hearing; ODAC voted 6-0 to withdraw at the hearing (earlier ODAC 12-1). Re-verified on federalregister.gov and govinfo.gov (77 FR 11554, FR Doc. 2012-4424). NOTE: source_id uses the E2100 NCT as the checkable trial anchor because the schema requires a PMID/NCT/DOI form; the fabricated 'DOI:10.1056/federalregister-2012-4424' was removed. The authoritative regulatory citation is 77 FR 11554 / FR Doc. 2012-4424 given in the citation field.

baseline.text: Yes. Adjuvant trastuzumab is one of the best-established survival-improving therapies in oncology. The pivotal HERA and joint NSABP B-31/NCCTG N9831 trials (both NEJM 2005) showed large disease-free survival benefits, and long-term follow-up plus meta-analyses confirmed a roughly one-third reduction in the risk of death, translating to a ~6-8 percentage-point absolute overall-survival gain at 10 years. It is standard of care in every major guideline (NCCN, ASCO, ESMO), with cardiotoxicity as the main manageable trade-off.

gate_trace.detail: 6 trial-grade on-population study(ies) on the claimed outcome
trial evidence adequate to assess
trial evidence agrees: effect present

ledger.citation: Piccart-Gebhart MJ, et al. Trastuzumab after adjuvant chemotherapy in HER2-positive breast cancer (HERA/BIG 1-01). N Engl J Med. 2005;353(16):1659-72. DOI:10.1056/NEJMoa052306
ledger.finding: Primary endpoint DFS: 1 year of trastuzumab vs observation, HR 0.54 (95% CI 0.43-0.67, P<0.0001), absolute 2-yr DFS benefit 8.4 points. At this first interim analysis (median 1 yr) OS was NOT yet significantly different (29 vs 37 deaths); the primary endpoint (DFS) is met but the CLAIMED OS outcome was still immature here, hence outcome_match=false for OS at this timepoint. Confirmed against PubMed abstract.
ledger.integrity_note: No retraction or integrity concerns; landmark phase 3 RCT, NCT00045032. Verified via PubMed: article types include 'Randomized Controlled Trial, Phase III'; no 'Retracted Publication' tag.

ledger.citation: Romond EH, et al. Trastuzumab plus adjuvant chemotherapy for operable HER2-positive breast cancer (joint NSABP B-31 & NCCTG N9831). N Engl J Med. 2005;353(16):1673-84. DOI:10.1056/NEJMoa052122
ledger.finding: Combined analysis of two RCTs: adding trastuzumab reduced DFS events HR 0.48 (P<0.0001) AND produced a 33% reduction in risk of death (P=0.015) at first interim analysis. Directly measures a mortality/OS endpoint in addition to DFS, both favoring trastuzumab. Effect sizes match PubMed abstract exactly. (n_int is an approximate single-arm figure; total joint analysis was larger.)
ledger.integrity_note: No retraction; pivotal joint analysis of two phase 3 RCTs (NCT00004067, NCT00005970). Verified via PubMed article types; no retraction tag.

ledger.citation: Perez EA, et al. Four-year follow-up of trastuzumab plus adjuvant chemotherapy: joint analysis of NCCTG N9831 and NSABP B-31. J Clin Oncol. 2011;29(25):3366-73. DOI:10.1200/JCO.2011.35.0868
ledger.finding: At median 3.9 years, sustained highly significant DFS benefit (P<0.001) and a statistically significant 39% reduction in death rate favoring trastuzumab (P<0.001) — confirms the OS benefit is durable, not just an early DFS signal. Matches PubMed abstract exactly.
ledger.integrity_note: No integrity concerns; mature follow-up of pivotal RCTs. PubMed article types: Phase III RCT; no retraction tag.

ledger.citation: Perez EA, et al. Trastuzumab plus adjuvant chemotherapy: planned joint analysis of overall survival from NSABP B-31 and NCCTG N9831. J Clin Oncol. 2014;32(33):3744-52. DOI:10.1200/JCO.2014.55.5730
ledger.finding: Definitive planned OS analysis (median 8.4 yr): 37% relative OS improvement, OS HR 0.63 (95% CI 0.54-0.73, P<0.001), 10-yr OS 75.2%->84%; DFS HR 0.60 (10-yr DFS 62.2%->73.7%). Directly and definitively measures the CLAIMED OS endpoint. All figures match PubMed abstract exactly.
ledger.integrity_note: No integrity concerns; pre-specified definitive OS analysis (710 events reached). No retraction tag in PubMed.

ledger.citation: Cameron D, et al. 11 years' follow-up of trastuzumab after adjuvant chemotherapy in HER2-positive early breast cancer: final analysis of the HERA trial. Lancet. 2017;389(10075):1195-1205. DOI:10.1016/S0140-6736(16)32616-2
ledger.finding: At median 11 years, 1 year of trastuzumab vs observation significantly reduced DFS events (HR 0.76, 95% CI 0.68-0.86) and death (HR 0.74, 95% CI 0.64-0.86). 2 years gave no additional benefit over 1 year (HR 1.02, 95% CI 0.89-1.17). Mature OS confirmation despite substantial crossover diluting the effect. Matches PubMed abstract exactly, including n_int=1702 (1-year arm).
ledger.integrity_note: No integrity concerns; final analysis of pivotal RCT (NCT00045032). PubMed confirms 884 (52%) of observation arm crossed over to trastuzumab, biasing the OS estimate toward the null, yet benefit persisted. No retraction tag.

ledger.citation: Early Breast Cancer Trialists' Collaborative Group (EBCTCG). Trastuzumab for early-stage, HER2-positive breast cancer: a meta-analysis of 13,864 women in seven randomised trials. Lancet Oncol. 2021;22(8):1139-1150. DOI:10.1016/S1470-2045(21)00288-6
ledger.finding: IPD meta-analysis of 7 RCTs (13,864 women, median 10.7 yr): breast-cancer recurrence RR 0.66 and breast-cancer mortality RR 0.67 (95% CI 0.61-0.73, P<0.0001); absolute 10-yr breast-cancer mortality reduced 6.4% and all-cause mortality reduced 6.5%, with NO increase in death without recurrence. Directly measures cause-specific and all-cause mortality. All figures match PubMed abstract exactly.
ledger.integrity_note: No integrity concerns; collaborative individual-patient-data meta-analysis, highest tier of evidence. PubMed article type 'Meta-Analysis'; no retraction tag.

ledger.citation: Moja L, et al. Trastuzumab containing regimens for early breast cancer. Cochrane Database Syst Rev. 2012;(4):CD006243. DOI:10.1002/14651858.CD006243.pub2
ledger.finding: Pooled 8 RCTs: trastuzumab significantly improved OS (HR 0.66, 95% CI 0.57-0.77, P<0.00001) and DFS (HR 0.60, 95% CI 0.50-0.71, P<0.00001). Independent systematic-review confirmation of OS benefit; cardiotoxicity is the recognized trade-off but does not negate the survival gain. Matches PubMed abstract exactly.
ledger.integrity_note: No integrity concerns; Cochrane systematic review/meta-analysis of 8 RCTs (11,991 patients). Also documents key harm: increased CHF (RR 5.11) and LVEF decline (RR 1.83). PubMed article types 'Meta-Analysis, Systematic Review'; no retraction tag.

baseline.text: Yes — low-dose colchicine reduces cardiovascular events in coronary disease. COLCOT (2019) and LoDoCo2 (2020), two positive NEJM RCTs, showed roughly 23-31% relative reductions in major cardiovascular events, and in 2023 the FDA approved colchicine (Lodoco) for cardiovascular risk reduction.

trial evidence adequate to assess
large RCTs themselves conflict

ledger.citation: Tardif JC, et al. Efficacy and Safety of Low-Dose Colchicine after Myocardial Infarction (COLCOT). N Engl J Med. 2019;381(26):2497-2505. DOI:10.1056/NEJMoa1912388. NCT02551094.
ledger.finding: Post-MI patients (within 30 days), N=4745, median 22.6-mo follow-up. Primary composite (CV death, resuscitated cardiac arrest, MI, stroke, or urgent hospitalization for angina leading to revascularization) occurred in 5.5% colchicine vs 7.1% placebo; HR 0.77 (95% CI 0.61-0.96), P=0.02. Primary MACE endpoint met - supports claim.
ledger.integrity_note: Landmark double-blind placebo-controlled RCT (PubMed article_types: Randomized Controlled Trial, Multicenter Study); no retraction or integrity concerns. Government of Quebec funded. Verified against PubMed abstract.

ledger.citation: Nidorf SM, et al. Colchicine in Patients with Chronic Coronary Disease (LoDoCo2). N Engl J Med. 2020;383(19):1838-1847. DOI:10.1056/NEJMoa2021372. ACTRN12614000093684.
ledger.finding: Chronic coronary disease, N=5522, median 28.6-mo follow-up. Primary composite (CV death, spontaneous MI, ischemic stroke, or ischemia-driven revascularization) occurred in 6.8% (187 pts) colchicine vs 9.6% (264 pts) placebo; HR 0.69 (95% CI 0.57-0.83), P<0.001. Primary MACE endpoint met - strongest single-trial support; matches claimed population and outcome.
ledger.integrity_note: Landmark double-blind placebo-controlled event-driven RCT; basis for FDA LODOCO approval. No integrity concerns (no retraction flag in PubMed). Signal of higher non-CV mortality (HR 1.51, CI 0.99-2.31) confirmed in abstract but CV endpoint robust.

ledger.citation: Jolly SS, et al. Colchicine in Acute Myocardial Infarction (CLEAR SYNERGY / OASIS-9). N Engl J Med. Online-first Nov 2024; print 2025;392(7):633-642. DOI:10.1056/NEJMoa2405922. NCT03048825.
ledger.finding: Post-MI, N=7062 (104 centers, 14 countries), median 3-yr follow-up. Primary composite (CV death, recurrent MI, stroke, or unplanned ischemia-driven revascularization) 322/3528 (9.1%) colchicine vs 327/3534 (9.3%) placebo; HR 0.99 (95% CI 0.85-1.16), P=0.93 - fully NEUTRAL. CRP still lowered (-1.28 mg/L) confirming pharmacologic engagement, but no MACE benefit. Contradicts claim on the identical primary endpoint.
ledger.integrity_note: Largest colchicine CV trial to date; 2x2 factorial, double-blind, CIHR-funded (PubMed article_types: Clinical Trial Phase III, Randomized Controlled Trial, Multicenter Study). No integrity concerns. NEJM online-first Nov 2024, print issue Feb 2025. Directly tempers earlier positive trials.

ledger.citation: Tong DC, et al. Colchicine in Patients With Acute Coronary Syndrome: The Australian COPS Randomized Clinical Trial. Circulation. 2020;142(20):1890-1900. DOI:10.1161/CIRCULATIONAHA.120.050771. ACTRN12615000861550.
ledger.finding: ACS patients, N=795 (396 colchicine, 399 placebo), 12-mo follow-up. Primary composite (all-cause death, ACS, ischemia-driven urgent revascularization, non-cardioembolic ischemic stroke): 24 vs 38 events, P=0.09 (NOT significant). Higher total death in colchicine arm (8 vs 1, P=0.017), driven by non-CV death (5 vs 0, P=0.024). Null on primary MACE - does not support claim.
ledger.integrity_note: Multicenter (17 Australian hospitals) double-blind placebo-controlled RCT; underpowered (N=795). No integrity concerns (no retraction flag) but flagged higher total/non-CV death in colchicine arm. Verified against PubMed abstract.

ledger.citation: Pinheiro L, et al. Long-term colchicine therapy in acute coronary syndromes: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials. Monaldi Arch Chest Dis. 2025. DOI:10.4081/monaldi.2025.3566.
ledger.finding: Long-term (>=12 mo) colchicine post-ACS. Composite of CV death/MI/revascularization/stroke NOT significantly reduced: HR 0.80 (95% CI 0.59-1.07, I2=73%). All-cause mortality HR 1.01 (0.67-1.53), CV death HR 1.01 (0.80-1.29), MI HR 0.86 (0.71-1.05) - all non-significant. Pooled estimate is null once the large neutral trial is included - key evidence for the Contested verdict.
ledger.integrity_note: Pooled COLCOT, COPS, CLEAR SYNERGY (12,602 patients; search date Dec 22 2024). High heterogeneity (I2=73% for composite) limits certainty. Lower-tier journal but standard PRISMA RCT meta-analysis. No retraction flag in PubMed. Abstract figures verified verbatim.

ledger.citation: FDA LODOCO (colchicine 0.5 mg) prescribing information, approved June 2023; Agepha Pharma. Indication derived from LoDoCo2 (NEJMoa2021372) plus supportive studies. DailyMed setid ff06d68f-d65f-d097-e053-6294a90a7e5f.
ledger.finding: FDA approved LODOCO (June 2023) to reduce risk of MI, stroke, coronary revascularization, and CV death in adults with established atherosclerotic disease or multiple CV risk factors - the first anti-inflammatory atheroprotective CV therapy. Efficacy basis was LoDoCo2 (31% RRR, HR 0.69, NNT 36). A standing US regulatory endorsement of the claim; however issued before the large neutral 2024/2025 trial.
ledger.integrity_note: Regulatory artifact, NOT a study - design='systematic review' is a schema-fit compromise (closest available enum), openly disclosed. Confirmed via DailyMed (setid matches), Agepha PI, TCTMD, Healio. Included as a standing regulatory data point: FDA-approved indication predates the neutral CLEAR SYNERGY readout, which is central to why consensus is Contested rather than Not Supported.

what_would_change_it: A definitive large RCT (n≥1000), or a current meta-analysis of RCTs, agreeing with one side would resolve the conflict.

ledger.citation: Reis 2022 New England Journal of Medicine
ledger.n: 1358 in the ivermectin-vs-placebo comparison (679 ivermectin, 679 placebo); 3515 randomized across all TOGETHER platform arms, mITT
ledger.finding: TOGETHER platform RCT: early ivermectin in ~3,500 symptomatic high-risk outpatients did not reduce hospitalization/prolonged ED observation vs placebo; no benefit.
ledger.integrity_note: Large double-blind placebo-controlled adaptive platform trial; no integrity concerns.

ledger.citation: Hayward 2024 Journal of Infection
ledger.finding: PRINCIPLE platform RCT (8,811 community adults): ivermectin gave no clinically meaningful faster recovery (HR ~1.15, below pre-specified 1.2 threshold) and no difference in hospitalization/death or 6-month recovery.
ledger.integrity_note: Large NIHR-funded open-label adaptive platform trial; no integrity concerns.

ledger.citation: Lim 2022 JAMA Internal Medicine
ledger.finding: I-TECH RCT (490 high-risk mild-to-moderate patients, Malaysia): ivermectin did not prevent progression to severe disease (21.6% vs 17.3%) and showed no secondary-outcome benefit.
ledger.integrity_note: Investigator-initiated multicenter RCT; no integrity concerns.

ledger.citation: Marcolino 2022 BMC Infectious Diseases
ledger.n: 14 ivermectin-vs-placebo RCTs (of 25 in the full review)
ledger.finding: Systematic review/meta-analysis of RCTs: ivermectin showed no significant effect on mortality, mechanical ventilation, or clinical improvement ('evidence beyond the hype' is null).
ledger.integrity_note: Post-hype synthesis; no integrity concerns.

ledger.citation: Zein 2021 Diabetes & Metabolic Syndrome
ledger.finding: Early meta-analysis (RCTs, ~1,788 patients) reported ivermectin associated with reduced mortality; this pooled benefit was driven by trials later withdrawn/flagged (Elgazzar, Niaee) and does not survive clean re-analysis.
ledger.integrity_note: The meta-analysis itself is not retracted, but its positive signal depended on primary studies later withdrawn/questioned; illustrates fragility of the early pro-ivermectin evidence.

ledger.citation: Elgazzar 2020 Research Square (preprint)
ledger.finding: Widely-cited preprint RCT claimed a large ivermectin mortality reduction and underpinned early positive meta-analyses. WITHDRAWN by Research Square (14 Jul 2021) for data-integrity/ethical concerns: duplicated patient records, deaths recorded before enrollment, and plagiarism.
ledger.integrity_note: Preprint withdrawn by Research Square for data-integrity/ethical concerns; never peer-reviewed yet drove early positive meta-analyses. Corroborated by Nature (d41586-021-02081-w) and multiple outlets.

ledger.citation: Shakhsi Niaee 2021 Asian Pacific Journal of Tropical Medicine
ledger.finding: Multicenter RCT (180 hospitalized adults) reported ivermectin sharply cut mortality vs controls; a positive study that fed pro-ivermectin meta-analyses. Data sleuths and an editorial note raised concerns over implausible baseline stratification/randomization; it is excluded from post-scrutiny meta-analyses.
ledger.integrity_note: Concerns raised informally (data sleuths, editorial note) over implausible baseline stratification; NOT a formal Expression of Concern — the journal stated the paper was not retracted and no retraction was pending. The formal EoCs were issued on downstream reviews (Kory; Bryant/Lawrie, Am J Ther), not on this primary study.
